dossier_meta.catalog_title: Star chromatic index of cubic graphs
dossier_meta.authors: Dvorak, Zdenek, Mohar, Bojan, Samal, Robert
dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: The star chromatic index $ \chi_s'(G) $ of a graph $ G $ is the minimum number of colors needed to properly color the edges of the graph so that no path or cycle of length four is bi-colored. Question Is it true that for every (sub)cubic graph $ G $ , we have $ \chi_s'(G) \le 6 $ ?
dossier_meta.context_text: The star chromatic number is the more usual concept [ACKKR,FRR]. Star chromatic index of a graph $ G $ is simply the star chromatic number of the line graph $ L(G) $ ; the definition given above is easily seen to be equivalent. Dvořák, Mohar, and Šámal [DMS] show that every (sub)cubic graph $ G $ , satisfies $ \chi_s'(G) \le 7 $ ? On the other hand, it is simple to check that $ \chi_s'(K_{3,3])=6 $ , so the conjecture, if true, is tight.
